title: a spec preflight round shows on the board and in the voyage like any reviewer at work, labelled as a preflight, without counting as a review round
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-04 three spec preflight rounds (actors such as reviewer-nikhil-sp-t189-r1b) ran for about ten minutes each, but the board's crew list and the 2.5D voyage showed only firstmate. The preflight path (`fm-review.sh --spec-preflight`, which sources bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh at fm-review.sh about 89-91) runs its own flow and writes no event: `grep sp-t189 state/events.jsonl` finds nothing. The board and the voyage build their crew from the event log (board/server.ts, `lastByActor`, about 1115-1137). The captain asked for preflight rounds to be visible ('好 加進去', 2026-10-04).

Visible. bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh is sourced before fm-review.sh defines `emit` (about 140-173), so it emits on its own through `fm-emit.sh`, using only existing neutral types (no new event type; both are already in fm-emit.sh:115-118 TYPES and fm-diagram.sh:124-128 ROUTINE).
Who the crewman is. Every preflight event carries the same identity payload a reviewer's events carry (bin/fm-review.sh:119-125): `data.crew_name` set to `$NAME`, and `data.identity` set to `$(fm_crew_identity)` (bin/fm-config.sh:587-592), read fresh from the run's identity.json under `$FM_RUN_DIR`. That is name, role, project, task, round, attempt, vendor, model_requested, model, cli_version, model_mismatch and vendor_resolution. The board takes a crewman's name, vendor, model and round from these fields (board/server.ts:1072-1074, :1182-1205). Without them it falls back to `legacyName(actor)` (:200-201), which would show 'nikhil-sp' with an unknown vendor and model. Every emit also passes `${project_events[@]}` (fm-review.sh:76-78, defined before the source at :89-91), so a `--project` preflight writes to that project's log.
Events:
- `crew_status`, sent at start and on progress, with `data.role='reviewer'`, `data.phase='review'`, `data.mode='spec-preflight'` and the identity payload above. The board then shows a review phase (board/server.ts about 1077, 1086-1091), and the voyage maps it to the lookout action (games/voyage-2d/src/board-source.js about 49-54).
- `agent_finished` when it ends, with the identity payload, `data.mode='spec-preflight'`, `data.preflight_outcome` set to one of `spec-ok`, `spec-gaps`, `refused`, `failed` or `interrupted`, and `data.result` set to `ok` for `spec-ok` and `spec-gaps` and `failed` for the rest.
Deriving the outcome. The exit code cannot separate the outcomes: SPEC-GAPS, a malformed final and refusals all exit 65 (bin/lib/fm_spec_preflight.py:134-135, :143-147; tests/spec-preflight-launcher.test.sh:59-66). The `finished` handler therefore reads the outcome from the evidence store. If a `spec-preflight` record for this run's actor (`$NAME`) and the spec's sha256 (`$FM_SPEC_PREFLIGHT`) was retained (`retain`, fm_spec_preflight.py:71-81, writes it before the exit-65 path), its `verdict` gives `spec-ok` or `spec-gaps`. With no retained record:
- exits 129, 130 and 143 are `interrupted`;
- an exit before `fm_run_chain` started (the 64, 65 and 70 exits at fm-spec-preflight.sh:16-31, :41, :46-61) is `refused`;
- any other exit is `failed`.
No task card from a preflight. The board's task list today adds every task id it sees in the event log (board/server.ts:878-883). Events of preflight actors are skipped in that loop. Preflight normally runs on a spec whose task file is not on main yet. If no definition or non-preflight event names the task, the task gets no card and never enters `/api/state` tasks, so the voyage never shows one either (board-source.js:37). The crewman still shows in the crew list, which carries its task id as text.
Which actors are preflights. Preflight-ness is a property of the actor, never of its latest event, because other emitters write under a preflight's actor without `data.mode`: the sandbox login-fallback warning (`fm_sandbox_board_warn`, bin/fm-sandbox.sh:164-170, through `fm_herdr_emit_status`, fm-config.sh:868, and `fm-herdr.py emit_status`, :2441-2470). Two rules:
- `fm-herdr.py emit_status` adds `data.mode` whenever the run's identity.json carries `mode` (identity.json records `mode: spec-preflight` at fm-herdr.py:551), so a sandbox warning mid-preflight is still marked.
- Every consumer decides by the actor: the board builds the set of preflight actors as those with any event whose `data.mode` is 'spec-preflight' (the preflight's own first `crew_status` always carries it), and `fm-herdr.py` decides from the run's identity.json `mode` (`state/runs/<actor>/identity.json`).
Label and hidden round, in all four places a round shows. The crew entry gains `mode`, set from that actor set in the crew builder near board/server.ts:1180-1192, where `round` is set at :1189. A preflight's identity.json still has `round=1` (fm-herdr.py:500, :549-551), so the round is hidden wherever `mode` is 'spec-preflight' and the label shows in its place:
- the roster row (board/public/ship.js:504-505);
- the crew card bubble and detail card (ship.js:150-169), with ship.js's own crew mapping (:215-240) passing `mode` through;
- the task card's crew chip (board/public/index.html:312-315); the task-card crew mapping at server.ts:1215-1217 passes `mode` along with id, name, role, round and attempt;
- the roster's round sort key (ship.js:477), which treats a preflight as having no round (-1).
The project-less view's field allow-list (server.ts:1339-1342) gains `mode`, so the label survives aggregation. The label is a new i18n key: 'spec preflight' (en) and '預檢' (zh-TW). Both 預 and 檢 are already in i18n/tw2cn.tsv (lines 113 and 93), so zh-CN shows '预检' without touching that table. When the round finishes, the crewman leaves the crew list exactly like a finished review round.
The trap. In bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh, the EXIT trap at :34 (today `trap 'fm_record_end "$?"' EXIT`) and the INT, TERM and HUP traps at :35-37 move up to immediately after `fm_identity` succeeds (:15). The EXIT trap becomes `trap finished EXIT`. That is before the first `crew_status` emit and before every exit at :16-31, so each exit after allocation emits the closing `agent_finished` (the rule fm-review.sh:213-215 states: 'Armed where emit() first works'). Exits before `fm_identity` (:6-14) happen before any emit and board nobody. The `finished` function calls `fm_record_end` with the exit status, derives the outcome as above, and emits `agent_finished`. It keeps today's behaviour of retaining the isolated checkout on interruption (the comment at :32-33). This satisfies the lint in tests/traps.test.sh:150-165 and :249-250, :268-270, which requires literally `trap finished EXIT` in any bin script that emits with its own --actor and --task. The INT, TERM and HUP traps stay exit-only.

Not a review round, not a task stage. Today's review-round counters already count only `review_opened`, so neutral events leave them unchanged: `fm-herdr.py` review_round about 378-399, `fm_autopilot_loop.py` about 211, `fm-ready.sh` about 142-143, `fm_merge_authorization.py` about 59-63, and the voyage's `live.js` reviewRounds about 20-32. Gate 7 reads stored evidence, not events. A test proves each stays unchanged. Every consumer of the events a preflight does produce treats `mode='spec-preflight'` as follows:
- `fm-herdr.py` `retire_dead_crew` (about 1912-1965) reads the dead actor's identity.json `mode` and, for a preflight, writes `data.mode` onto the `agent_lost` for that process, and does not push the `lost: <task> <actor>` wake onto state/session/wake.jsonl or ring firstmate's doorbell for it (the push at fm-herdr.py:1955-1959; bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:563-570). firstmate started the preflight and reads its log; a dead preflight leaves no verdict there.
- The board never moves a task's stage, blocks it, or shows a lost round because of any event of a preflight actor, including `agent_lost` and a failed `agent_finished` (server.ts about 869 and 924). It only drops the crewman.
- The board's handoff `peer()` (board/server.ts:1093-1097) excludes preflight actors from its candidates, so a live preflight is never the `to` end of a `pr_opened` handoff and never makes a `review_opened` or `pr_opened` ambiguous.
- The autopilot (`bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py` about 493-510) queues no 'Round lost' or 'Round failed' wake for any event of a preflight actor; it recognises the actor by any of its events carrying `data.mode` 'spec-preflight' (never by an actor-id pattern, which an ordinary alias such as `zain-sp` can mimic). The preflight's own caller (firstmate) reads its result.
- `fm-herdr.py` `retire_dead_crew` also writes the closing `agent_finished` with `status: 'process_gone'` that follows each loss (:1960-1967). For a preflight it carries `data.mode` too. No consumer reads the mode from that closing event: the board already hides it from the log (server.ts:1218-1229) and only drops the crewman.
- `fm_watch.py` `inflight` (:642-664) counts any actor with `data.role` 'reviewer' whose last event is not `agent_finished` as crew in flight. A live preflight therefore counts. That is intended: firstmate started it and waits on its result. While it runs, firstmate's Stop and turn-end hooks keep it parked with the park text (:725-729, :758-760, :806-816) instead of ending the turn, exactly as for a live review. The day-long wait's exit code 2 is the same. Its closing `agent_finished`, emitted by the `finished` trap or by `retire_dead_crew` after a kill (:1960-1967), clears it. No change to fm_watch.py.
A task's first real review after any preflights is still round 1.

Design. Two numbered sections are edited, each in place, following the design rule: a change goes into the numbered home section of the contract it changes, and is never appended at the end of design.md.
- §8 (The captain's board): the crew liveness table row and rule that describe `agent_lost` (design/design.md:1698 (liveness row) and :1735-1752 (rule 5, Liveness) and :1696-1698) say that a preflight's loss only removes the crewman; the crew contract gains the preflight label, the hidden round number, the rule that preflight events add no task card, and that `peer()` ignores preflight actors.
- §11 (Self-update): the deck-reconcile paragraph (design/design.md:2620-2626) and the 'Waking the harness (T-137)' list of pushes (:2751-2758) say that a lost preflight writes `agent_lost` and its closing `agent_finished` carrying `data.mode`, and pushes no `lost:` wake.
The T-185 preflight section (design/design.md:1262-1296, or wherever T-189 moves it) describes preflight records and dispatch rules, not the board, and is left unchanged.

Migration. No actor-id pattern is used to recognise a preflight: a reviewer alias such as `zain-sp` can produce an ordinary id in the same shape (bin/fm-review.sh about 56, bin/fm-herdr.py about 433 and 532-538). A preflight actor is one that has any event with `data.mode = 'spec-preflight'`, as the board and the voyage read it. `retire_dead_crew` and `emit_status` instead read the run's identity.json `mode`. Every event a preflight run writes carries the mode. That includes `fm_sandbox_board_warn`'s `crew_status`, which goes through `fm_herdr_emit_status` (bin/fm-config.sh about 868-875) to `fm-herdr.py` `emit_status` (about 2441-2470). `emit_status` adds `data.mode` from the run's identity.json, so neither bin/fm-sandbox.sh nor bin/fm-config.sh changes. No past preflight events exist: `state/events.jsonl` has 0 events from any `-sp-` actor (checked 2026-10-05), and no ordinary-name preflight runs exist in any registered project's state. So no legacy rule is needed. A test allocates an ordinary review with the alias `zain-sp`, kills it, and checks that it keeps its lost mark and its autopilot wake. Another test checks that the preflight's own sandbox-warn event carries the mode.

Voyage reviewer lookup, closing the preflight gap. `games/voyage-2d/src/board-source.js` gives preflight crewmen a distinct marker (for example `preflight: true`). `games/voyage-2d/src/director.js`'s reviewer lookup (about 154-157), used by the rituals at about 222-223, 234, 241 and 248-249, skips crewmen with that marker. A preflight still shows as a lookout but never receives a real review's `pr_opened` scroll or approval ritual. A voyage test covers a worker and a preflight live on the same task with `pr_opened`.

Vendor and model, closing the preflight gap. Before its first emit, the preflight records the head vendor and the requested model exactly as a review does: `fm_record_requested` after the vendor is resolved, mirroring fm-review.sh about 113-115. So the start `crew_status` carries them. The preflight also passes a `prepare` callback to `fm_run_chain` (8th argument, fm-config.sh about 725 and 773-776), which `fm_run_chain` calls before every attempt (fm-config.sh about 725 and 773-776), including the first. Each attempt's `crew_status` carries that attempt's vendor and requested model, so a fallback shows the fallback vendor. These are the only 'progress' emits. The test checks that the start `crew_status` carries the head vendor and requested model, and that a fallback re-emits with the fallback vendor.
